solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Salient point from Conservative leaving sales talk

indicators.note: leaving means departing, so the C walks out of the word

blocks.note: C = Conservative, taken out of PITCH

explanation.surface: A political commentator picks out the key point once the Tory stops his sales patter.
explanation.walkthrough: C is the standard abbreviation for Conservative.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the soft core of a fruit gives the figurative sense of the central, most telling part of an argument.

clue.text: Musical agent dealing with Topsy-Turvy supports one not working

indicators.note: upside down: in a down entry the letters read bottom to top
in a down entry, what supports sits underneath, so the reversed block goes below I

blocks.note: a rep is a sales agent

explanation.surface: A theatrical agent handling the Gilbert and Sullivan film Topsy-Turvy is propping up an out-of-work actor.
explanation.walkthrough: Topsy-Turvy is a real film about Gilbert and Sullivan, so it passes for the title of the musical; it is only the instruction to turn the first three words upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a machine or rule that has stopped functioning or has no effect is described this way.

clue.text: Fiery primate conceals archbishop’s first difficult issue

indicators.note: to conceal is to hide, so POTTO hides the A inside it
take only the opening letter of archbishop

blocks.note: a potto is a small African primate
first letter of archbishop, placed inside POTTO

explanation.surface: A hot-tempered churchman hides the archbishop's first awkward problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Primate' wants to be a senior bishop, which suits archbishop; it is the animal, a potto.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: something too awkward to handle, passed quickly from person to person like a scalding vegetable.

clue.text: Peter hit cops extremely tentatively in protective gear

indicators.note: to cop is to catch, so SAFE BELT catches the letters inside it
take the two extreme letters of tentatively

blocks.note: peter is old criminal slang for a safe

explanation.surface: A man called Peter lashes out at police, though only half-heartedly, while wearing riot gear.
explanation.walkthrough: Peter looks like a man's name; in crosswords and old underworld slang it is a safe, hence a safecracker is a peterman.
explanation.definitionFit: A strap worn in cars and aircraft to restrain passengers during a crash counts as equipment that protects.

clue.text: Some fail regularly following split

indicators.note: at regular intervals, so take every other letter of fail
following means coming after, so these letters are placed after the split

explanation.surface: Some people keep failing after a break-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' looks like the start of the surface sentence, but it is the whole definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both words stand before a plural noun for an unspecified handful, more than two but not many.

clue.text: This topic should be avoided in Bedford

blocks.note: IN BEDFORD rearranged, that is ground up

explanation.surface: A local warning that some subject is taboo in the town of Bedford.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram indicator is the answer's own second word: FORBIDDEN is IN BEDFORD ground, crushed and remixed, so the answer describes its own wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: territory you may not enter, extended to a subject that conversation must steer around.

clue.text: More neat French gentlemen in German city

indicators.note: in means inside, so the gentlemen stand within the city's letters

explanation.surface: Some Frenchmen in a German city are more smartly turned out.
explanation.walkthrough: MM is the French abbreviation for Messieurs, gentlemen.
explanation.definitionFit: A comparative adjective: trim describes something tidy and well kept, and this form means more so.

clue.text: Bird, say, on top of tree

indicators.note: in a down entry, the top of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A bird perches at the very top of a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' looks like a preposition about perching; it gives RE, meaning concerning.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by class: a white wading heron, one kind of bird among thousands.

clue.text: Dryer in tall building changing hands

indicators.note: right hand is swapped for left: R becomes L

blocks.note: a tower; its R (right) changes to L (left)

explanation.surface: A clothes dryer is installed in a tower block that has just been sold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Changing hands' reads as being sold; here the hands are right and left, R and L.
explanation.definitionFit: A cloth used after bathing removes water from skin, so it is literally a thing that dries.

clue.text: Barman’s driven me to Barking

indicators.note: barking means mad, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A publican complains that his customers have driven him to Barking, the London suburb.
explanation.walkthrough: Barking looks like the east London district; it is barking mad. A barman in crosswords is a composer, someone who writes bars of music.
explanation.definitionFit: A crossword-only sense: an Italian composer of madrigals and operas wrote his music in bars, so he is a barman.

clue.text: Vaunted team

blocks.note: boasted, the old past tense of crow
a group working together, on a ship or film set

explanation.walkthrough: 'The cock crew' is the older past tense of crow, and to crow is to boast or vaunt.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic past tense of crow, to brag loudly, and also the people who work a ship or film set together.

clue.text: Impressionist in US city starts to impersonate Romney

indicators.note: the starts of words are their first letters

blocks.note: first letters of impersonate and Romney

explanation.surface: A comic impressionist in an American city is about to do an impression of Mitt Romney.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's impressionist is a mimic, which suits impersonate; the answer is the painter.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the French painter of Luncheon of the Boating Party belonged to the movement of Monet and Degas.

clue.text: Great time to enter base

indicators.note: to enter is to go in, so the time letter goes inside the base word

explanation.surface: A fine moment arrives to set foot in the base camp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Base' looks like a noun, somewhere to enter; it is the adjective, morally low.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose synonym: figures whose fame will never die, like sporting or literary legends, are called great.

clue.text: Why battery’s replaced in holiday resort

indicators.note: the letters are put back in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone on holiday wonders why the battery has been changed.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder's two Ys and odd consonants point to Welsh spelling once you think of place names.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a university town on Cardigan Bay in west Wales, popular for seaside breaks.

clue.text: Tennis legend finishing early for nothing

indicators.note: the word stops one letter short

blocks.note: Rafael NADAL without his last letter

explanation.surface: A tennis great retires early and gets nothing for it.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface nods to Nadal's actual retirement; 'finishing early' is literal, his name cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: A regional use: Spanish for zero, borrowed into American slang.

clue.text: Light source shone out, constraining very exposed part of Tyrolean ensemble?

indicators.note: out means wrong or disordered, so SHONE is rearranged
to constrain is to hold in, so the outer parts hold ER between them
exposed means stripped of covering, so very loses its outer letters

explanation.surface: A spotlight picks out the most revealing part of an Alpine band's costume.
explanation.walkthrough: Ensemble reads as a band of musicians; it is an outfit, and the question mark flags a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Leather shorts with braces are one garment of traditional Alpine dress, so they are one piece of the outfit.

clue.text: Getting better of those people interrupting continuously

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break in, so the pronoun breaks into the phrase for continuously

blocks.note: them = those people, inside ON END

explanation.surface: Someone recovering gets irritated by visitors who keep butting in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting better of' reads as defeating someone; 'of' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: a patient recovering from illness, or a situation improving, is said to be this.

clue.text: Clergyman’s trifling argument against accepting article

indicators.note: to accept is to take in, so the argument word takes the article inside

explanation.surface: A vicar raises a petty objection to taking on an item.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Article' reads as an item or piece of writing; in crosswords it is a, an or the.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by class: a priest attached to a cathedral who assists at services but is not on its governing chapter.

clue.text: Smooth-talker in good spirits losing heart to member

indicators.note: the middle letter is given up in exchange for what follows

blocks.note: cheer = good spirits; its middle E goes
an arm is a limb, a member; it takes the E's place

explanation.surface: A smooth operator in high spirits loses his heart to a club member.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Losing heart to' reads as falling in love; it means the heart of the spirits word is swapped for the member.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: someone who wins people over with flattery and easy conversation.

clue.text: Close match one’s seen in bed

blocks.note: a tie is a match, as in a cup tie

explanation.surface: A tight game being watched from bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close match' reads as one tight game; split it. A cup tie is a British term for a knockout match.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic hint: a woman's loose nightdress is the garment commonly worn when sleeping.

clue.text: In Kyoto, your hat might be made of this

definitions.text: hat might be made of this

indicators.note: the answer lies inside the next words

explanation.surface: A tourist in Kyoto is told what local hats are made from.
explanation.walkthrough: Toyo is a Japanese straw-like material, so the surface's setting is the answer's origin too.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a shiny rice-paper straw from Japan woven into summer hats.

clue.text: Elegant socialite broadcasting

explanation.surface: A stylish society girl is on the radio.
explanation.walkthrough: A debutante is a young upper-class woman launched into society, shortened to deb.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: suave, stylish and confident in manner, usually said of a man.

clue.text: Doctor can up quantity of saliva

indicators.note: in a down entry, up reads bottom to top

blocks.note: can is slang for a toilet, a loo

explanation.surface: A doctor is able to raise the amount of spit collected for a sample.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can' looks like a verb; it is the toilet, American slang, and a loo is the British word.
explanation.definitionFit: A noun use: the spit that dribbles from a baby's or dog's mouth.

clue.text: Start living, having raised grand

indicators.note: in a down entry, the G is lifted higher up the word

blocks.note: BEING with its G taken out
G = grand, a thousand; put back higher, after BE

explanation.surface: Someone starts a new life after coming into a thousand pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: The G never leaves the word: BEING has its G moved up two places.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both verbs mean to set something going or take the first step.

clue.text: Arrive at nursing home, to begin with, in distinct part of town

indicators.note: GET TO holds H like a nurse holding a patient
only the first letter of home

blocks.note: first letter of home, inside GET TO

explanation.surface: Visiting a care home in a separate neighbourhood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nursing home' reads as a care home; nursing is the container and home gives only its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a district where one minority group lives, set apart from the rest of the city.

clue.text: Some sleazy groper lying about in meeting of Congress

indicators.note: part of the words holds the answer
about turns the letters round

explanation.surface: A political scandal: a sleazy congressman lying about groping.
explanation.walkthrough: Congress, capitalised to look like the US legislature, is sexual intercourse.
explanation.definitionFit: A pun: congress in its old sense is sex, so a wild group session is a gathering for it.

clue.text: Unknown number in Scotland know cycling in High Peak

indicators.note: the first letter of AMOUNT goes round to the end
KEN and Y go inside MOUNTA

blocks.note: AMOUNT with its A cycled to the back

explanation.surface: Hikers in the Peak District come across an unknown number of Scots cycling.
explanation.walkthrough: High Peak is a real district of Derbyshire, which disguises the definition: a high peak.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Africa's second-tallest mountain, an extinct volcano on the equator.

clue.text: Win card game in Panama?

blocks.note: to land a prize is to win it

explanation.surface: Winning at cards while wearing a Panama hat.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a definition by example: the isthmus of Panama joins two continents.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the isthmus is a narrow strip joining North and South America.

clue.text: After party, nearly obtains port in Qatar

indicators.note: nearly means not quite all, so the word falls one letter short

blocks.note: HAS, which means obtains, without its last letter

explanation.surface: After a party someone almost reaches a Gulf port.
explanation.walkthrough: A do is British slang for a party or celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the capital city lies on the Gulf coast and serves as the country's main harbour.
